name: Chronophotography
summary: A series of photographs, or many exposures on one plate, that split a movement into steps and lay the steps side by side.
how: Record 12 to 24 frames each second, or 5 to 20 exposures on one plate.
Hold the camera and the dark ground still; the body moves against a plain field.
Show each stage of the movement in a form that overlaps its neighbour by 20% to 50%.
In a painting, repeat a limb or a form along the path of the movement.

origin.note: Eadweard Muybridge records a galloping horse with a row of cameras; Étienne-Jules Marey takes many exposures on one plate from 1882.

adoptions.via: Étienne-Jules Marey makes his chronophotographic gun and fixed plate in Paris.
Anton Giulio Bragaglia publishes photodynamism, a blurred photograph of movement.
Giacomo Balla paints Dynamism of a Dog on a Leash with repeated legs and tail.
Marcel Duchamp paints Nude Descending a Staircase No. 2 in stages.

sources.title: Marta Braun, Picturing Time: The Work of Étienne-Jules Marey (University of Chicago Press, 1992)
Giacomo Balla, Dynamism of a Dog on a Leash (1912)
